quest.title: Until Vana is Healed
quest.description: You wonder how Ararycan is doing. Go find him when you have the time.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are you, Ararycan? We're here to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon? *sob*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Judging from Ararycan's look...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something's wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't tell Paimon the forest is "sick" again?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Paimon guessed it. The bad guys that wish to make Vana sick came back. Ararycan couldn't fight them off alone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The bad guys keep coming around, and we can't always stay in the woods like Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only there's a surefire solution...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: "Surefire"? Is that a name of a mushroom Ararycan doesn't know about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If there was a mushroom you could devour to solve all problems, I'd be the first to chomp it down!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still got to rely on ourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, "surefire" means you do something once to solve a problem permanently.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: No mushroom is that powerful. Even the Lord of Dendro and Aramuhukunda can't do that. Neither can Varuna Contraption, who got sick twice from the bad stuff.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: An easy way out like that is a pipe dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True... but how are we going to solve this problem?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If the bad guys keep coming back, no way we can show up every time Ararycan needs our help.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Maybe Nara has an idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Which Nara? Oh, right, Jazari mentioned he's researching the Ruin Golem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he wasn't making headway until we finally got into the Ruin Golem with him last time.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: No, not that Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ararycan rejected that so decisively! But other than Jazari, we don't know anyone else who's studying the Ruin Golem.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows another Nara, Nara Pir Kavikavus. He might know something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Nara Pir Kavikavus"? Where has Paimon heard that name before...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, Jazari said Pir Kavikavus is a genius of Kshahrewar and delved into the Ruin Golem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But he also said Pir Kavikavus got into an accident on an expedition and all his key findings were lost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Was Ararycan...?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan doesn't understand what Paimon said. Ararycan just know Aralohita, the Aranara accompanied Nara Pir Kavikavus in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pir Kavikavus could see Aranara? And they traveled together?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not to mention that he was an academic genius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that practically makes him the main character in a story! If only not for the accident...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I guess that's why the good die young.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In contrast, Jazari couldn't even see Ararycan, and looked at Paimon with pity!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was obviously talking to Aranara, but he thought Paimon was rambling to herself.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Aralohita likes riddles and traps, but he can't be found now...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Though where he stayed before probably has the "solution" that {NICKNAME} mentioned.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows the place, but it's got new Marana. Very dangerous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #By "Marana," you mean The Withering? Don't worry, you let Nara {NICKNAME} handle that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since we don't have any other leads, we'll have to check it out.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan will take you there! But be careful, bad guys that wish to make Vana sick are probably not too far away.

choices.text: If we get the Akademiya to help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even they can't make something that powerful... Otherwise, there wouldn't be any scholars tearing their hair out trying to write a thesis.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #The riddle is not hard. It is the order in which Nara {NICKNAME} saw Dusk Bird, Shroomboar, and Rishboland Tiger.

talks.objective: Go deeper into the cave to search for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do they still have their eyes on the Ruin Golem?

choices.text: They just don't know when to quit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I know, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, how did they find out about this place? What if they beat us to the clues?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Baddies aren't Aranara's friends so they won't find the "solution".

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Aralohita likes riddles and traps and hid the "solution." Bad guys aren't with Aranara so they won't get the answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even so, Paimon's still a bit worried... Let's hurry up to find the clues.

choices.text: They just don't give up, do they...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now's not the time to admire them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like Aranara was here for a while. On the wall, is that a message from Aralohita?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Aralohita left a riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It must be really hard...

choices.text: Can we solve it by force?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Uh, no, no violence against Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, what exactly is the riddle? And is the answer the "solution" we're looking for?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: No, the riddle is simple, that's why Aralohita hid the "solution" in the labyrinth. The passage to the labyrinth is the answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... We just have to solve the riddle and figure out the passage to the labyrinth first, right?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Paimon's right.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: The riddle is a short one. "Ran across it the day before yesterday, yesterday, and today..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Ran across it the day before yesterday, yesterday, and today..."? Eh? How are we supposed to guess that?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: What are "the day before yesterday," "yesterday," and "today"? Aralohita learned them from Nara, they are not Aranara words.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's right. Aranara doesn't really understand our concept of time. How can we explain it to Ararycan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, "today" runs from the most recent daybreak to dark. "Yesterday" is the same cycle before that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ..."Day before yesterday" is the one before that. Probably not the best way to describe it, but do you get it, Ararycan?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Yes... "Today," Ararycan met Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's correct, but probably not the answer to the riddle...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Aralohita wrote the answer in three different places. Let's look around.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps we should go straight to the end...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, if there are only three spaces to fill, maybe we can get them all right on our first try?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ararycan mentioned Aralohita likes mechanisms, b—but there shouldn't be any that would blow up when receiving wrong answers, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you know what Aralohita's mechanisms are like, Ararycan?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan has no idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh. Then we should be cautious. We don't want to lose important clues because of our screw-ups.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The answer are in three different places and shouldn't be far. Let's search those places!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Solving a riddle like this is nothing to {NICKNAME}.

talks.objective: Search for the answer(s) to the riddle
Search for the answer(s) to the riddle
Search for the answer(s) to the riddle

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the time of truth! Paimon's so afraid we'll botch this... Let's review the riddle again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Ran across it the day before yesterday, yesterday, and today..." So the answer is...

choices.text: The order of the answer is still unclear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We only know the answer includes Dusk Bird, Shroomboar, and Rishboland Tiger, but we don't know in what order they should be placed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How are we going to know what Aralohita ran across and on which day? Paimon thought you said it was an easy one, Ararycan!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Paimon... The riddle is not a question. It's not about Aralohita.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it if it's not a question? And who else can it be about if it's not about Aralohita? Mmm... Paimon's not getting this at all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We should probably think beyond the text.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... But normally, Aranara only understand literal meanings. Now there's an Aranara who can speak in riddles? Paimon can't keep up...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #The order. Not how Aralohita met them, but how Nara {NICKNAME} met them.

choices.text: Fungus, Sumpter Beast, and Golden Wolflord.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, Paimon doesn't think that's correct in any conceivable way!

talks.objective: Enter the "labyrinth" using the Rhythm of the Gloomy Path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Found it, finally! Is this a clue from Aralohita?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It looks like some sort of transcript... Oh, this must be the results of Pir Kavikavus's research! {NICKNAME}, let's read it now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm, let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Theory and Practice: Enhancing the Safety of the Chaos Core in Unstable Conditions Using the Khaenri'ah Ruin Golem of Devantaka Mountain as an Example"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what does that mean? Paimon knows these words but doesn't get it when they're put together like this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this an academic study...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This might be a long shot... but do you understand this, Ararycan?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Look like lots of crawling bugs. Yuck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, none of us understand it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll have to ask Jazari...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ararycan may not approve... but Pir Kavikavus has been gone for a long time, Aralohita too. Jazari's our only hope at this point...

choices.text: I don't think he'll have a good reason to refuse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. We might not understand it, but he'll definitely be interested in it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mr. Jazari is probably still on Devantaka Mountain researching. Since we have a lead now, let's go look for him.

choices.text: He'll probably be over the moon about it.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Nara Jazari is on moon? So, very far, cannot come here to help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! It's just a figure of speech, it means he'll be very, very happy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are, Mr. Jazari! It was not easy to find you.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's {NICKNAME} and... Paimon, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y-Yes, but why are you looking at Paimon like that?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, I'm worried about you. I don't know how you've been doing since the last time I saw you. Did you see a doctor...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh... You don't need to worry about that!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: (*sigh* Your friend's situation may seem fine now, but you'd better keep an eye on her.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey! Just because you're whispering to {NICKNAME} doesn't mean Paimon won't hear everything! There are no secrets between us! Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: *sigh* Okay, only the person wearing the shoes will know if they fit. Since you insist that you're fine, then there's nothing more I can say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Why does that sound so harsh?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Harsh? Sumeru people are warm and sincere. As one of them, I don't mean anything other than what I said.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Anyway, what brings you two here? Did you suddenly develop a passion for scholarship and finally decide to dedicate yourselves to the pursuit of truth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Well, it does have to do with scholarship... Take a look at this!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You give Jazari a look at the data you found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mr. Jazari? Hellooo?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (What's up with him? Is it even too hard for him to understand...?)

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: (Is Nara Jazari small iron chunk? Broken?)

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ah-Aaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! Why did you shout out of nowhere like that?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: My Pir Kavikavus... No, this is a paper by none other than Pir Kavikavus himself!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: And it's his "Theory and Practice: Enhancing the Safety of the Chaos Core in Unstable Conditions Using the Khaenri'ah Ruin Golem of Devantaka Mountain as an Example"?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: My stars, with such an exclusive, pioneering research in my hand, even if I just wrote a review, I could still apply for funding from the Akademiya!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Tell me, where did you find this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (We can't exactly tell him we found it in the Aranara labyrinth... Just make up some random answer...)

choices.text: We found it in a mushroom cave deep in the forest...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: What? Pir Kavikavus was conducting research in a place like that? Hmm... Looks like I'd better examine my own research attitude...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We tried reading it, but we couldn't make heads or tails of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: These are the results of some very important research, right? What's written in it? Could you give us the simple version, Mr. Jazari?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Why do you want to know about it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't Mr. Jazari say before that "the gates to scholarship will open to whoever has a seeking heart"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon also really wants to know what a genius like Pir Kavikavus wrote about.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I did say that... but... but I've been following this project for a very long time!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: If you must know, the amount of prior research I've done over the years is even more than the stories you've heard.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Th-This is a great discovery indeed, and you were the ones to find this important data...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Regardless, now that you've embarked on the path of scholarship, you are novices that will require my expertise to guide you through an accurate reading of this text...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: You... You won't try to publish your results before me, will you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why are you worried about that?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, such a publication would undoubtedly bring both fame and fortune. As they say, your fate isn't determined by your ability, but your luck.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: With your remarkably good luck... I don't think I would stand a chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Then you're worrying yourself over nothing. {NICKNAME} and Paimon don't have a permit from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We would never conduct research with malicious intent.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Is that so? Why didn't you say so! But worry not, if you ever want to seek an academic career, I'll write you a letter of recommendation.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: And by then, hehe, my letters of recommendation will be worth a fortune.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: For now though, there's no time to lose. Let's go to the core of the Ruin Golem to test Pir Kavikavus's theory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! This just might solve our problem, Ararycan! It may not be a permanent cure, but at least that takes care of the current crisis.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Yes! Nara Jazari not no good, is good!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Ah, you see, I'll soon become a wealthy researcher. To repay you... why don't I recommend a few good physicians to you for your self-talk?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon already said it's fine! Hmm... but Paimon would gladly welcome being treated to some more Sumeru delicacies.

choices.text: I woke up and discovered it in my bag...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Oooh! Why hasn't anything so wonderful ever happened to me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back... If we can completely seal the core, even the Abyss Order will have a hard time wrecking it again.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: My little friend, even if you don't have faith in me, you should have faith in Pir Kavikavus.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I read through his masterpiece several times on the way here. I completely understand it now...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: That's Pir Kavikavus, all right! A paragon of genius!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: It's unfortunate that such a genius no longer walks among us. However! He left behind a clear path. All we need to do is follow it to reach the correct destination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like there won't be much we can do to help, so we'll just have to count on you, Mr. Jazari!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. As they say, "Sword is the final solution." Still, I hope you can draw your weapon now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: "Roses have thorns, treasure troves have snakes." Who can say what perils await us.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Besides, this great endeavor mustn't be stopped halfway! If we're interrupted, not even Pir Kavikavus himself could predict the consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it really gonna be that dangerous!?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: It's possible that nothing will happen at all, and it's also possible that we'll end up buried here together. In any case, it's better to be safe than sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I have much faith in your abilities. When I seal the core, I'll trust you to cover my rear!

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Nara Jazari wants us to push his lower back? Ararycan wants to help, but Nara Jazari too tall, Ararycan can't reach.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He means that he wants us to guard this place and keep him from being interrupted by bad guys when he's sealing the core.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Great! Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is no time to mess with Ararycan! Mr. Jazari just wants us to guard this path so that he can focus on his task. Now all you need to do is stay put with us, Ararycan.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ah, just what I would expect from myself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D-Did it work?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Do I even need to say it? I am a Kshahrewar researcher who aspires to receive the Pir Kavikavus Prize, and I have guidance from Pir Kavikavus himself...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: If I couldn't succeed even with all that, it'd be hard to imagine anyone else from the Akademiya completing this task.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's impressive, Mr. Jazari!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: The original data from the previous study was already enough for a conventional publication, but now... Ahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ahem, my apologies, I lost my composure there for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Not only have records of Pir Kavikavus's long-lost research been recovered, but now I'm testing his theory, and it was a success. No matter how you put it, it's...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A great success!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Quite right, quite right! I'll have to publish on an even larger scale. With results like these, an upgrade is naturally reasonable, and I won't need to worry about research funds anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Most importantly, there hasn't been an academic breakthrough like this in many years, not since Kshahrewar was devastated by Pir Kavikavus's accident...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Now there's hope for reviving the Kshahrewar thanks to the rediscovery of Pir Kavikavus's research!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Goodness, it's so wonderful I can hardly believe it.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I should head back and record today's results while they're still fresh in my mind. If I have the opportunity to issue them publicly, I hope you'll both come to listen.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: After all, you have made a significant contribution to the project, and as its leader, I'm indebted to you. If you ever need any help, just come find me.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Even if I'm busy, I'll always spare some time for you two, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jazari leaves in a flash.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan not helpful at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean? Didn't you complete your mission? Now those bad things that made the forest sick are sealed away and those Abyss Order goons won't be able to do a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Using other people's strength is also wise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right, some things just can't be done by yourself. There's no shame in getting some help from others.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's important is that you're protecting what you want to protect.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: This mean Ararycan has protected Vana?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Even if it's not protected once and for all... at least you healed the forest's illness. Isn't that your contribution?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Yes! Thank you, Paimon, and thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}, Ararycan's friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Mr. Jazari still couldn't perceive Ararycan at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like he's a far cry from Pir Kavikavus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, and didn't he promise to treat us to some food from Sumeru? Darn it! We forgot to set a time and place... Paimon hopes we'll run into him again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How about you, Ararycan? Will you stay in Devantaka Mountain?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Bad guys gone, and the things that make Vana sick sealed now. All safe now.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan go back to Vanarana, tell other Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Ararycan will not forget Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Don't forget Ararycan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, of course we won't! And we'll definitely come back to Vanarana if we get the chance!

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Okay! Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Ararycan's friends!

talks.objective: Go to the end of the "labyrinth"
